sections.title: Letter uve doble
paragraphs: The name of this letter is (uve doble) /ˈdoble be/. Its main sound is heard in the word (web) /ˈweb/, which means web. This letter makes three different sounds in borrowed words.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: For the first sound, round your lips tightly and lift the back of your tongue. For the second sound, press your lips firmly together, stop the airflow, and release it with your voice. For the third sound, bring your lips close together without touching, and let the air flow smoothly between them. Touch your throat to feel your voice buzz for all three sounds.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: In borrowed words from English, this letter makes the sound /w/, like in (whisky) /ˈwis.ki/. In words from German, at the start of a word, it makes the sound /b/, like in (wolframio) /bolˈfɾa.mjo/ and (wagneriano) /baɡ.neˈɾja.no/. Between vowels in German borrowings, it makes the softer sound /β/, like in (kuwaití) /ku.βajˈti/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: You might want to touch your top teeth with your bottom lip, like in the English word vine. Spanish never uses teeth for these sounds. Keep your teeth completely away from your lips. When you say the soft sound, let air squeeze between your lips without closing them fully.
